solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Complicated logic I use to preserve previous purpose for Apple (6,9)

indicatorNotes.to preserve: the anagram keeps the other piece inside it, as a jar preserves fruit

blocks.note: previous = OLD, purpose = END (an end in view)

annotation.surface: Someone untangling the reasoning behind an Apple product, or the company's old mission.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital A makes Apple look like the tech company; it is the fruit, and the Golden Delicious is a variety of apple.
annotation.definitionFit: Golden Delicious is a well-known variety of apple.

entries.clue: Finally snap in rage, so agitated (2,5)

annotation.definition: Finally snap in rage, so agitated

indicatorNotes.Finally: finally points to the end of the word, so only its last letter is used
indicatorNotes.in: the P goes into the mixture

annotation.surface: Someone who has held it together until they finally snap in a fit of rage.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: it builds the letters and also describes what it means to go spare, British slang for losing your temper.
annotation.definitionFit: To go spare is British slang for becoming furious, exactly finally snapping in agitated rage.

entries.clue: Fencing’s bound to fall quickly if uncapped (5)

indicatorNotes.uncapped: with its cap, the top letter, taken off

blocks.note: to fall quickly = PLUNGE, minus its first letter P

annotation.surface: A claim that a fencing sport is doomed to decline fast if the protective tips come off the blades.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain to', but here it is a leap, and ''s' belongs to the definition, not a link.
annotation.definitionFit: A lunge is the forward thrust in fencing, a sudden bound at the opponent.

entries.clue: Add detail to meme’s content, like Clangers? (9)

indicatorNotes.content: a word's content is what sits inside it

annotation.surface: Adding a flourish to an internet meme about the Clangers, a British children's TV show.
annotation.walkthrough: The Clangers were knitted creatures in a 1970s British children's programme; here the word just means things that clang, so bells, and 'like' them is BELL-ISH.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to embellish is to decorate, so adding ornamental detail to a tale or design.

entries.clue: Day journal is a tedious thing (4)

blocks.note: a rag is a newspaper, usually a poor one

annotation.surface: A grumble that keeping a daily diary is dull.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Day journal' reads as a diary; split it, and 'journal' is a newspaper, which crosswords love to call a rag.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal sense: a drag is a bore, anything that drags on.

entries.clue: Sample of polite, rational, educated people (8)

indicatorNotes.Sample of: a sample is a small part taken from the words that follow

annotation.surface: A survey drawing on polite, rational, educated respondents.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma hides the join: the answer runs across 'polite' and 'rational'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the learned classes, from Latin for lettered men.

entries.clue: Maximum quota for fattened fowl (5)

blocks.note: a cap is an upper limit
on = for, as in a limit on something

annotation.surface: A limit on how many fattened birds a farmer may produce.
annotation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, 'a maximum quota for' is simply 'a cap on', and the two words run together into the bird.
annotation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated cockerel fattened for the table.

entries.clue: Prominent bust or bum one has (9)

indicatorNotes.bum: bum as an adjective means bad or faulty, so the letters are wrong

annotation.surface: A comment on whichever body part sticks out most.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bum' reads as a body part to pair with 'bust'; it is the adjective meaning dud, telling you to rearrange BUST OR. 'One has' is spoken as I'VE, one being I.
annotation.definitionFit: Something obtrusive sticks out, prominent in an unwelcome way.

entries.clue: Multitudes uprising advance endlessly as rich loaf (7)

indicatorNotes.uprising: in a down clue, rising means read bottom to top
indicatorNotes.endlessly: a word without an end has lost its last letter

blocks.note: advance (money) = LEND, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: Crowds rise up to share out a rich loaf.
annotation.walkthrough: Stollen is a German fruit bread eaten at Christmas.
annotation.definitionFit: Stollen is a rich fruit loaf, often with marzipan inside.

entries.clue: Roughly clean both sides of scab after the rest (9)

indicatorNotes.both sides of: the two outside letters of scab

blocks.note: the two sides of Scab are S and B, written S AND B
last = coming after all the rest

annotation.surface: Cleaning a wound's scab once everything else has been dealt with.
annotation.walkthrough: The trick is to write out 'both sides' in full: the sides are S and B, and the AND itself goes into the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: To sandblast is to clean a surface by blasting sand at it, a rough cleaning.

entries.clue: Terrace with partial occupation (5)

indicatorNotes.partial: only part of the next word is used

annotation.surface: A terrace, perhaps of houses, that is only partly lived in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Terrace' suggests a row of houses to go with 'occupation'; here it is paving outside one.
annotation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved terrace beside a house.

entries.clue: Ancient nameless ruin of Donegal (3-3)

indicatorNotes.nameless: without N, the abbreviation for name
indicatorNotes.ruin of: ruined letters are knocked into a new shape

annotation.surface: An old, forgotten ruin in County Donegal, in Ireland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ruin' looks like a noun for the old building in the scene; it is the instruction to wreck the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Something age-old is ancient, having existed for ages.

entries.clue: Composed question in letter from Athens, enveloped with scent (8)

indicatorNotes.in: Q goes inside the Greek letter
indicatorNotes.enveloped with: the scent wraps around what came before

blocks.note: a scent is the trail a hound follows

annotation.surface: A calmly written question in a perfumed letter posted from Athens.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'letter from Athens' is not correspondence but an alphabet letter, and 'scent' is the hound's sense of the word, the line it follows.
annotation.definitionFit: Composed and tranquil both mean calm and untroubled.

entries.clue: Latecomer in election takes the lead, sounding repetitive (6)

indicatorNotes.takes the lead: the last letter moves to the front

blocks.clueFragment: Latecomer in election takes the lead
blocks.note: election = CHOICE; its latecomer is its last letter, which goes to the front
election = choice, now without the E that moved up

annotation.surface: A late-declaring candidate surges ahead in an election, repeating the same lines.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Latecomer' is not a candidate but the last letter of CHOICE; move E to the front and CHOICE becomes ECHOIC.
annotation.definitionFit: Echoic means imitating or repeating a sound, like an echo.

entries.clue: Deeply experienced judge abandoned over time (9)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, over means turned upside down

annotation.surface: A seasoned judge who was deserted long ago.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deeply experienced' reads as 'very seasoned', which sits with the judge; it means deeply felt.
annotation.definitionFit: Heartfelt means felt deeply, and to experience is to feel, so deeply experienced is a fair paraphrase.

entries.clue: One taking place at back of stable? (8)

annotation.definition: One taking place at back of stable?

indicatorNotes.at back of: being at the back of something means coming after it, so ION follows STALL

blocks.note: a stall is a stable compartment
on = happening, as in 'the show is on'

annotation.surface: A horse settling into its place at the back of the stable.
annotation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue simply describes the horse in its stable, so the wordplay and the definition are the same sentence.
annotation.definitionFit: A stallion is an uncastrated male horse, just the sort of one kept at the back of a stable.

entries.clue: Some underwear in pine bathrooms (4,5)

blocks.note: to pine is to long for
john is American slang for a toilet

annotation.surface: Underwear left lying in bathrooms fitted out in pine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the wood of the bathroom fittings; it is the verb, to long.
annotation.definitionFit: Long johns are full-length thermal underpants.

entries.clue: Net weight nonstandard beer tin holds (8)

indicatorNotes.nonstandard: not in the standard order, so rearranged
indicatorNotes.holds: the rearranged letters hold W inside

annotation.surface: A label complaint: the net weight of this odd-sized beer can is not what it says.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Net weight' is a phrase from packaging; split it, and 'Net' is the internet, jokily called the interweb.
annotation.definitionFit: Interweb is a jokey name for the internet, the Net.

entries.clue: Try to poach bananas and the centre nearly splits (8)

indicatorNotes.bananas: bananas means crazy, so the letters go mad
indicatorNotes.nearly: nearly means not quite all, so the word stops one letter short
indicatorNotes.splits: HU goes into the middle of the rearranged letters

blocks.note: centre = HUB, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A kitchen disaster: poaching bananas until the middle splits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Poach' suggests cooking and 'bananas' fruit; poach means lure staff away, and bananas is crazy.
annotation.definitionFit: To headhunt is to try to poach staff from another firm.

entries.clue: Indifferent writer saying one could cut lead (7)

blocks.note: a hack is a mediocre writer
a saw is an old saying

annotation.surface: A mediocre writer claiming that one person could take the leading role.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as the leading role; it is the metal, which a hacksaw cuts.
annotation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed saw for cutting metal, such as lead.

entries.clue: Bearing north, take advantage of graphic directions as a turn-off (6)

annotation.definitionNote: 'a turn-off' is a noun; read 'as a turn-off' as describing something off-putting, which is adjectival

indicatorNotes.Bearing: bearing means carrying, so USE carries N inside it

blocks.note: to use someone is to take advantage of them
x and y are the two directions on a graph

annotation.surface: Heading north to exploit explicit instructions, which prove off-putting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Graphic' hints at explicit content, fitting the sexy theme; it means belonging to a graph, whose axes run x and y.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition read as 'being a turn-off' describes something off-putting, which is what unsexy means.

entries.clue: Vote for split when accounts are concluded? (4,3)

blocks.note: yea is a vote in favour
to rend is to split apart

annotation.surface: A vote to split up at the moment the books are closed.
annotation.walkthrough: The enumeration (4,3) invites YEAR + END; the wordplay breaks the letters at a different point.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by the question mark: closing the books is the most familiar thing that happens at the year end.

entries.clue: Made Urban withdraw to make jerk godly? (8)

indicatorNotes.withdraw: drawing back, the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: make godly = DEIFY, jerk = TIC: deify a tic

annotation.surface: Pope Urban backing away from turning a fool into a god.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital U makes Urban look like a pope; it is just the adjective. Deify the tic, then read the whole thing backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Cityfied means made urban, turned into or adapted to city life.

entries.clue: Unpreserved meat has changed hands (5)

indicatorNotes.has changed hands: the L (left hand) is swapped for R (right hand)

blocks.note: left becomes right: L swaps for R

annotation.surface: Meat that has been sold on without being cured.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Changed hands' sounds like a sale; here the hands are left and right, L and R.
annotation.definitionFit: Fresh food has not been preserved by salting, drying or tinning.

entries.clue: When I’m due in Paris I roughly pack things thrown out (6)

indicatorNotes.pack: ETA packs JE and C inside it

annotation.surface: A traveller heading for Paris packing things roughly and throwing some out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'When I'm due' is a travel abbreviation, estimated time of arrival, and 'roughly' is the Latin circa shortened to one letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical plural, used mainly of volcanic material or of matter blasted from a star.

entries.clue: Mufflers with ends trimmed cut into figure, possibly (5)

indicatorNotes.with ends trimmed: both end letters are cut off

blocks.note: mufflers = SCARVES, minus S and S

annotation.surface: Scarves trimmed at the ends and cut to flatter the figure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like a body shape to go with scarves; it is a statue you might carve.
annotation.definitionFit: To carve is to cut material into a figure, such as a statue.

entries.clue: Root is immature insect food (4)

blocks.note: to root about is to dig around in the soil
a larva, the soft young stage of a beetle
informal slang for something to eat

annotation.surface: A root that is food for young insects.
annotation.walkthrough: There are really three definitions here: to root, a larva, and food.
annotation.definitionFit: To grub is to root around; grub is also slang for food, and a larva.

entries.clue: Podcaster’s influenced kid (5)

indicatorNotes.Podcaster’s: a podcaster speaks, so this is what you hear

annotation.surface: A podcast host has swayed a child.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kid' reads as a child being influenced; it is kid leather, goatskin, and suede is another soft leather.
annotation.definitionFit: Kid is soft goatskin leather, and suede is similar soft napped leather, often kid.

entries.clue: Toiler’s poorer when accommodating old king, King Henry (9)

indicatorNotes.accommodating: WORSE makes room for the kings inside

blocks.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the physics unit of inductance

annotation.surface: A labourer is worse off for having to put up the old king, Henry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'King Henry' looks like one monarch; it is two abbreviations, K and H, the henry being a unit in physics.
annotation.definitionFit: A workhorse is someone who does a lot of hard toil.

entries.clue: Have a wee one after having a wee one? (3,3,5,4)

annotation.definition: Have a wee one after having a wee one?

blocks.note: the surface pushes a trip to the toilet; the setter means have a wee (Scots: small) drink
the second wee one is a newborn baby

annotation.surface: A trip to the toilet after something small, or a small drink after a birth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Have a wee one' suggests a toilet visit; the first is a wee dram, the second a wee (Scots for small) baby. To wet the baby's head is the British custom of drinking to a newborn.
annotation.definitionFit: Wetting the baby's head means having a celebratory drink after a baby is born.
